prompts: This is an instructional notebook. It introduces the adult census dataset and demonstrates the essential data exploration steps that precede any machine learning workflow, with the goal of building intuition about the data before modeling. Key takeaways include: (1) distinguishing numerical columns (e.g., age, capital-gain, hours-per-week) from categorical columns (e.g., workclass, education, occupation) and understanding why this distinction matters; (2) using pandas methods such as head, value_counts, and crosstab, and seaborn plots (hist, pairplot, scatterplot) to inspect distributions and relationships; (3) recognizing data issues such as class imbalance in target_column ('class') and redundancy between education and education-num; and (4) understanding how hand-crafted threshold rules on age and hours-per-week foreshadow decision tree logic. Expected outputs include: adult_census loaded as a DataFrame, numerical_columns and categorical_columns lists defined, all_columns used to subset the data, histogram and pairplot visualizations, and a scatterplot with manual decision boundaries. The education-num column is intentionally dropped because it is perfectly redundant with the categorical education column; keeping the categorical version is preferable for subsequent models that handle heterogeneous features, since it avoids the implicit assumption that education levels have a linear effect on the target outcome. If asked about more information on the dataset, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/datasets_adult_census.html
